I shall decide issue no.4, pertaining to territorial jurisdiction first, which is reproduced below: 4. Whether the suit filed by the Plaintiff lacks territorial jurisdiction? OPD KLA Foods India Ltd. Vs. Field Fresh Foods Pvt. Ltd. (Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd.) CS DJ No.618253/2016 Page 44/74 45 Kla Foods India Ltd vs Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54063058/ 35 64. As per clause 12 of the LOI Ex. PW-1/3 / DW-4/2, the parties have agreed that the courts at Delhi shall have exclusive jurisdiction. The law with respect to exclusive jurisdiction in contracts has been stated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in A.B.C. Laminart (P) Ltd. v. A.P. Agencies, (1989) 2 SCC 163 at page 172: "16. So long as the parties to a contract do not oust the jurisdiction of all the courts which would otherwise have jurisdiction to decide the cause of action under the law it cannot be said that the parties have by their contract ousted the jurisdiction of the court. If under the law several courts would have jurisdiction and the parties have agreed to submit to one of these jurisdictions and not to other or others of them it cannot be said that there is total ouster of jurisdiction. In other words, where the parties to a contract agreed to submit the disputes arising from it to a particular jurisdiction which would otherwise also be a proper jurisdiction under the law their agreement to the extent they agreed not to submit to other jurisdictions cannot be said to be void as against public policy. If on the other hand the jurisdiction they agreed to submit to would not otherwise be proper jurisdiction to decide disputes arising out of the contract it must be declared void being against public policy. Would this be the position in the instant case?" KLA Foods India Ltd. Vs. Field Fresh Foods Pvt. Ltd. (Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd.) CS DJ No.618253/2016 Page 45/74 46 65 . Therefore, clause 19 of the LOI would apply only if the courts at Delhi have territorial jurisdiction to entertain the present suit. Kla Foods India Ltd vs Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54063058/ 36 Section 18 CPC refers to place of institution of a suit where local limits of jurisdiction of courts are uncertain; whereas, Section 19 CPC contemplates suits for compensation for wrongs to person or movables; Section 20 CPC, is the residuary provision, which provides that suits which do not come within the purview of Sections 16 to 19 of the Code are to be instituted where the defendants reside or cause of action arises. Therefore, Section 20 CPC applies where neither a right relating to immovable property, nor a wrong done to a person or movable property is involved. Thus, the suit can be instituted before any of the three courts having territorial jurisdiction as contemplated under Section 20 of the Code, i.e., where 'cause of action' has arisen, or where KLA Foods India Ltd. Vs. Field Fresh Foods Pvt . Ltd. ( Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd.) Whereas in the case of 'repudiation of contract', the place where repudiation is received is the place where the suit would lie. CS DJ No.618253/2016 Page 47/74 48 Court has held as below: 15. The determination of the place where the contract was made is part of the law of contract. But making of an offer on a particular place does not form cause of action in a suit for damages for breach of contract. Ordinarily, acceptance of an offer and its intimation result in a contract and hence a suit can be filed in a court within whose jurisdiction the acceptance was communicated. The performance of a contract is part of cause of action and a suit in respect of the breach can always be filed at the place where the contract should have been performed or its performance completed. If the contract is to be performed at the place where it is made, the suit on the contract is to be filed there and nowhere else. In suits for agency actions the cause of action arises at the place where the contract of agency was made or the place where actions are to be rendered and payment is to be made by the agent. Part of cause of action arises where money is expressly or impliedly payable under a contract. In cases of repudiation of a contract, the place where repudiation is received is the place where the suit would lie. If a contract is pleaded as part of the cause of action giving jurisdiction to the court where the suit is filed and that contract is found to be invalid, such part of cause of KLA Foods India Ltd. texts.arguments: In para no.30 of the plaint, the plaintiff claims that the present court has jurisdiction since (i) the cause of action has arisen within the territorial jurisdiction of this Court, (ii) the transaction between the plaintiff and the defendant took place in New Delhi, and (iii) that the negotiations leading up-to the execution of the agreement took place in New Delhi and (iv) the office of the plaintiff is also in New Delhi. 21. Thus, the plaintiff claims an amount of Rs.51,60,641/- from the defendant as compensation for the cost of cold storage and other related damages, as the frozen green peas were sold at a loss to a third party by the plaintiff, along with costs of the suit. In the written statement, the defendant raised a preliminary objection with respect to the territorial jurisdiction of this Court to KLA Foods India Ltd. Vs. Field Fresh Foods Pvt. Ltd. (Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd.) CS DJ No.618253/2016 Page 10/74 Kla Foods India Ltd vs Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54063058/ 8 11 entertain the present suit. Further the plaintiff was required to supply the frozen peas from its plant in Rudrapur and the contract was also to be performed at Rudrapur. 23. The defendant further raised a preliminary objection that there was a breach of contract on the part of the plaintiff as the product did not meet the statutory requirements as prescribed under section 21 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2010 read with the Food Safety and Standards Regulations 2011, which provide that no food article shall contain microbiological counts in excess of the stipulated limits. Hence, the defendant has submitted that there cannot be an agreement for sale and purchase of food products which are not safe and not fit for human KLA Foods India Ltd. Vs. Field Fresh Foods Pvt. Ltd. (Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd.) CS DJ No.618253/2016 Page 11/74 12 consumption as all food products have to statutorily comply with various provisions provided under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and now the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2010. Kla Foods India Ltd vs Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54063058/ 9 24. Acting on the representation of the plaintiff's representatives, a team of the defendant company visited the plaintiff's facility at Rudrapur, Uttarakhand and samples of frozen green peas were picked up from the stocks available, which were found to meet the physical, chemical and microbiological standards of food safety laws and those of the defendant. 26. As per para no.2 of the preliminary submissions of the KLA Foods India Ltd. Vs. Field Fresh Foods Pvt. Ltd. (Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd.) CS DJ No.618253/2016 Page 13/74 14 defendant, the plaintiff company had assured and warranted that the frozen green peas to be supplied to the defendant shall be in strict conformity with the chemical and micro biological standards as provided for by food safety laws. 27. As per para no.3 of the preliminary submissions of the defendant, Appendix D - Table 2 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and Appendix B - Table 4 of the Food Safety and Standard Regulations, 2020 categorically provide for the micro-biological parameters with respect to the frozen vegetables and every entity engaged in the business of frozen fruits and vegetables has to unconditionally ensure the conformity Kla Foods India Ltd vs Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54063058/ 11 and compliance of its product with the parameters as set out in the food safety laws, therefore the plaintiff was under an obligation to ensure that frozen peas supplied by it to the defendant should be in absolute conformity with the microbiological parameters. As per the defendant, after much efforts and discussion, the plaintiff agreed that the defendant can get the frozen peas tested KLA Foods India Ltd. Vs. Field Fresh Foods Pvt. Ltd. (Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd.) CS DJ No.618253/2016 Page 20/74 21 for conformity with micro biological parameters and other Kla Foods India Ltd vs Del Monte Foods Pvt. Ltd on 27 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54063058/ 18 highlighted in the said mail that it was due to non-testing of the frozen green peas for ensuring conformity with statutory requirements that had led to delay and requested the plaintiff not to go ahead for arranging the inspection of old stocks. As per the defendant, absolute compliance with quality parameters as provided under law was must besides ensuring the traceability of the material under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 41. Further the plaintiff denied that the consignment of frozen peas contained microbiological counts in excess of tolerance limits as specified in the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 or the Food Safety and Standards Regulation 2011. Further the defendant stated that if the goods did not meet the specifications and statutory requirements, it would not be accepting the material at all.
